headline: サンキュー is borrowed from English thank you.
Kasumu is from Old Japanese and cognate with 霞める (kasumeru, “to blur, to obscure”) and かすか (kasuka, “faint, dim”).
Mashi is the continuative stem of the verb 増す (masu).
Omonjiru is a shift from the verb 重んずる (omonzuru), as -uru verbs moved to the -iru pattern.
ロープ is borrowed from English rope.
Fukureru is from Old Japanese 膨る (pukuru), and the source compares 袋 (fukuro, “bag”), from the way a bag is filled with items.
Ware is from Old Japanese, the long form of 我 (wa) plus れ (-re, nominalizing suffix).
